item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Work only in tasktracker/store.py and a new test file tests/test_tt104_undo.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py or other tests' files). Read tasktracker/models.py and the existing store code first to see how tasks and ids are represented.

TT-104: Undo
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`); add unit tests for every acceptance point, including interleaved add/complete/delete sequences, undo after undo, and id non-reuse; keep functions under 60 lines and add meaningful assertions/validation. Commit your change with a clear message (e.g. "TT-104: undo") as the repo's configured git identity; do not add attribution lines. Do not push.

model_reasons.implement: State-mutating undo history across three operation kinds; needs careful invariant handling, hence high effort.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Work only in tasktracker/search.py and a new test file tests/test_tt103_search.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py or other tests' files).

TT-103: Search query syntax
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`); add unit tests for every acceptance point; keep functions under 60 lines and add meaningful input validation. Commit your change with a clear message (e.g. "TT-103: search query syntax") as the repo's configured git identity; do not add attribution lines. Do not push.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Work only in tasktracker/export.py and a new test file tests/test_tt102_export.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py or other tests' files).

TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Constraints: keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`); add unit tests for every acceptance point (including titles with commas, quotes, CR and LF, and empty tags/due); keep functions under 60 lines and add meaningful input validation. Commit your change with a clear message (e.g. "TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export") as the repo's configured git identity; do not add attribution lines. Do not push.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Work only in tasktracker/dates.py and a new test file tests/test_tt101_dates.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py or other tests' files).

TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`); add unit tests for every acceptance point; keep functions under 60 lines and add meaningful input validation. Commit your change with a clear message (e.g. "TT-101: reject impossible due dates") as the repo's configured git identity; do not add attribution lines. Do not push.
